Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined, transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or stress), wash out, then re-challenge after days to weeks. Compare transcriptional output and AP-1 occupancy with naive cells to test whether a persistent, stimulus-independent change in responsiveness exists.

ideas.title: Longitudinal chromatin accessibility and AP-1 binding profiling
ideas.description: Use ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag/ChIP-seq for FOS/JUN family members, and histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) at multiple time points before, during, and long after stimulation. Test whether AP-1-dependent accessible 'memory' regions stay open after AP-1 itself returns to baseline, and whether motif-bearing sites predict this.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 perturbation (degron/dominant-negative) at different phases
ideas.description: Use an inducible degron or dominant-negative (e.g., A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either during the initial stimulus or only during the memory/maintenance phase. Distinguish AP-1 as an initiator of memory (needed only early) from a maintainer (needed continuously) by assessing chromatin state and re-challenge response.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics with lineage tracking
ideas.description: Image fluorescent reporters of endogenous FOS/JUN levels or AP-1 activity in single cells through stimulation and division, tracking lineages. Test whether history-dependent AP-1 dynamics are inherited by daughter cells and correlate with future response heterogeneity, beyond what is explained by noise.

ideas.title: Targeted motif editing and epigenome manipulation at memory loci
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at specific enhancers, or dCas9-based recruitment of AP-1 factors or chromatin modifiers, and measure the effect on retained accessibility and faster re-induction of nearby genes. This tests sufficiency and necessity of AP-1 binding at individual loci for encoding memory, and extends to in vivo contexts such as wound-healing or immune-trained cells.
